name: Specimen sheet
source: A botanical-plate title film: a cut-out subject on a light technical grid with registration dots, red specimen labels, callout crops linked by connector lines and corner handles, tiles of detail crops, images inside the cut-outs of oversized wide caps, a dotted halftone dissolve, and a line-art trace. Red, black and pale grounds. Described from a contact sheet; no files or pixels are carried.

frame_device.what: A drafting sheet: hairline grid lines (solid and dashed), small registration dots at crossings, a circle or arc construction line around the subject, and small label tags ('SPECIMEN_01', 'Surface_02') in a wide-tracked class. Annotated crop boxes carry four corner handles (small squares) and connect to the subject with thin lines.
frame_device.moves: The grid is drawn on first (lines draw out, dots pop), then the subject lands inside it; callout boxes spawn from the subject, resize and tile; lines re-route (0.5 s expo.inOut) as the boxes move; at section changes the whole sheet re-colours (pale to red to black) while the grid persists.

ground_motion: The grid paper drifts: the ruling and the paper tone slide 6 to 12 px and a few percent of tone over 10 s, and the registration marks tick, so a hold on the sheet still moves.

type.classes: Title: a wide extended sans in caps (regular to medium weight, 4 to 8% tracking), large; label: small wide-tracked caps or mono on a coloured tag; callout caption: tiny sentence-case with a connector.
type.behaviour: Titles are whole and readable at rest, the same height as the cut-out beside them. A title may split (letters spread apart) so that an image crop sits inside the gap or inside a letterform, but at rest the line reads as one phrase in full. Labels pop on with their crop and never overlap the title.

image.treatment: A cut-out subject (transparent edges) on the grid, plus rectangular detail crops of it that show on the sheet with handles and labels. Crops can fill the counters of letters, tile in a row, or be recoloured (a blue variant, a greyscale variant, a line trace).
image.behaviour: The subject is never a rectangle photo: it is the cut-out with its own shadow-free edge. Crops are born from a region of the subject (a box is drawn, then lifts out, then resizes to a tile). Images in letterforms hold the crop's scale while the word moves across them.

transitions: crop box lifts out of the subject and becomes the next scene's tile
tile row slides and resizes into one letterform image
colour swap of the whole ground (pale to red to black)
halftone or dot dissolve of the subject
title letters spread to open a gap for the next image

techniques.name: Grid draw and registration
techniques.what: Hairline grid lines draw out, registration dots pop at crossings, a construction circle sweeps around the subject.
techniques.route: SVG lines with stroke-dashoffset (0.6 s power2.out, 0.05 s stagger), dashed lines via stroke-dasharray 4 4, dots scale 0 to 1 (0.2 s back.out(3)); a circle with stroke-dashoffset drawn once in 0.9 s.

techniques.name: Cut-out landing
techniques.what: The cut-out subject lands on the sheet with a small rotation settle and its label tag pops beside it.
techniques.route: PNG with alpha (the real product or object, cut by media-use background removal): y 40 to 0 and rotate -4 to 0 (0.7 s expo.out), label tag scale-x 0 to 1 (0.25 s power3.out).

techniques.name: Crop callout with handles
techniques.what: A box is drawn on a region of the subject, four corner handles appear, a connector line follows, and the crop lifts out as a labelled tile.
techniques.route: A div with a 1 px border over the region (clip-path inset to zoom the same image at 2.4x inside), four 6 px squares at the corners, an SVG line from the box to the subject point that updates in onUpdate; lift by y and scale (0.5 s expo.out).

techniques.name: Tile row and resize
techniques.what: Several crops sit in a row on the sheet, sliding and resizing in a stagger, linked by thin arcs.
techniques.route: A flex row of clip-path windows with GSAP Flip (or manual width tweens) staggered 0.06 s (0.6 s expo.inOut); curved connectors as SVG paths with dashoffset draws.

techniques.name: Image inside a letterform
techniques.what: A crop fills the gap or the counter of a wide capital in the title, so the picture is part of the word.
techniques.route: Set the word with the letter replaced by an inline-block box sized to the glyph, holding the crop; or background-clip: text on one letter with the crop as its background; the crop's scale held while the box moves.

techniques.name: Title spread
techniques.what: The title's letters part on the beat, the crop moves through the gap, and the title closes up again.
techniques.route: Split letters; tween x of the left group negative and right group positive by 12 to 18% of the width (0.5 s expo.inOut), the crop moves through, then back to 0 with a 0.3 s power3.out; the word reads whole at rest.

techniques.name: Ground colour swap
techniques.what: The whole sheet changes colour in one beat (pale, red, black) while the grid and the subject stay.
techniques.route: A ground div background tween 0.25 s power2.inOut; CSS variables for the grid line and label colours updated in the same set so contrast holds (ink on ground at 4.5:1).

techniques.name: Halftone dissolve
techniques.what: The subject breaks into a dot or bar pattern that drifts off, handing the frame to the next view.
techniques.route: A canvas or SVG pattern mask: mask the subject with a dot grid whose circle radius tweens from 0 to cell size (0.8 s power2.inOut) or reverse; flat films use a stepped dot grid of solid dots.

techniques.name: Line-art trace
techniques.what: The subject is redrawn as a line drawing, a stroke tracing its contours in the ink colour.
techniques.route: SVG paths (traced from the subject's silhouette or the real icon) with stroke-dashoffset over 1.4 s power1.inOut; fill fades out 0.3 s as the strokes draw; for UI, trace the real component outlines.

techniques.name: Specimen label tags
techniques.what: Little tags name each crop (SPECIMEN_01, Surface_03, Receptacle), numbered in order, so the sheet reads as a catalogue.
techniques.route: Small divs with a filled background in the accent, mono or wide caps at 1.1% frame height, popped by scale-x 0 to 1 from the left edge (0.2 s) 0.1 s after their crop lands; numbering from a counter.

techniques.name: Specimen turns on its label axis
techniques.what: The cut-out specimen rotates in real 3D about the axis its label sits on, the callout labels staying pinned to the same points.
techniques.route: Rasan3D: the real object as a GLB or an image on a `k.pxPlane` stack (3 to 5 layers, 0.04 apart) with `k.material("matte")`; rotation.y 0 to 0.9 rad over 1.4 s power3.inOut about the label axis; labels are DOM, pinned with `k.toScreen` in `onDraw` and hidden when not visible; even `top-soft` light, no shadow, no DOF.

techniques.name: Line-art trace lifts into a wireframe
techniques.what: The 2D line trace of the specimen lifts off the sheet and becomes a wireframe in space that turns once, then flattens back to the trace.
techniques.route: Rasan3D: `THREE.LineSegments` (or `k.tube` for the strokes) built from the same traced paths with a z-depth per contour; `LineBasicMaterial` in the ink colour, 1 px; the group rotates 0 to 0.7 rad and z-depth lerps 0 to 1 over 1.0 s power3.inOut, back over 0.8 s; from the `grid-draw` frame (`k.layout`) so the lift is the same drawing.

techniques.name: Sheet folds in real space
techniques.what: The paper sheet the specimen sits on folds along its grid line and the camera pulls back from it, no gloss and no shadow.
techniques.route: Rasan3D: a `k.pxPlane` split in two halves hinged on the grid line, hinge rotation 0 to 1.2 rad over 0.9 s power3.inOut, `k.material("paper")` kept matte (or unlit), `window` rig soft; camera pos pulls back 12% with a 70 mm lens; no bloom.

techniques.name: Word choreography
techniques.what: Each word of the line enters from its own place (its own offset, scale and blur) and settles into the line with a gentle lift, instead of typing on letter by letter; the key word arrives last and lands with a little more overshoot.
techniques.route: Split the line into word spans; GSAP from each word's own x/y offset (24 to 80 px, different per word), scale 0.88 to 1.15 and blur 6 to 12 px to rest, 0.55 s, stagger 0.09 s; end with a 4 to 8 px lift settling back (y -6 to 0) on back.out(1.4) or an elastic.out(1, 0.7) tail; every word readable at rest and the line whole before the next line starts; the next line's first word starts 0.2 s before this line's last settles (overlap).

signature: A crop box lifts out of the subject, grows handles, and becomes the next scene's tile or the picture inside the title's letter.

density.note: A new crop, tile, title move or colour swap about every 1.2 s; the grid and labels are constant, so the sheet always feels annotated.

palette.ground: pale cool grey (#F1F0F3), cut to red (#D4192A) and black (#050505)
palette.ink: black on pale, white on red and black
palette.accent: one saturated red; an unrelated cool colour (blue) may appear only inside crops
palette.note: A brand palette overrides these; the devices stay. The cut-out and crops carry the product's real colour.

do: Draw the grid first, then land the subject
Give every crop a handle set, a label and a connector
Use the real product or object as the cut-out and crops
Keep the title whole and readable at rest
Change the ground colour on a beat to reset the eye
Use wide, airy caps and generous space around the subject
dont: Do not use stock photos or invented objects
Do not crop the title at rest or cover it with a crop
Do not let connectors cross each other
Do not add drop shadows, glow or blur
Do not use more than one accent colour on the sheet
fits: launch ladder (each rung a crop and a label)
explainer for physical or visual products
